literal: Among wisdom all chief they say, evil things even to those who harm not doing refraining.
translation: They say the foremost of all wisdom is to refrain from doing evil, even to those who harm you.
modern: தமக்குத் தீங்கு செய்பவர்க்கும் தீமையான செயல்களைச் செய்யாமல் இருப்பதே எல்லா அறிவுகளிலும் சிறந்த அறிவு என்று கூறுவர்.
explanation: This couplet defines the highest form of wisdom in the context of fearing evil deeds. The phrase 'அறிவினுள் எல்லாம் தலை' establishes a hierarchy of knowledge, placing moral restraint at the very top as the 'head' or chief wisdom. The word 'செறுவார்க்கும்' means 'even to those who harm or hate', emphasizing that retaliation is never justified. Finally, 'செய்யா விடல்' highlights that true wisdom is not merely theoretical, but the active, disciplined choice to refrain from committing evil regardless of the provocation.
